suggestions.reason: All five assertions also pass in the without_skill arm, so this eval as written cannot discriminate skill value. The repo's CLAUDE.md already documents both the i18n parity rule and the e2e-when-web-changed rule, so the baseline has the same knowledge; what actually differed was efficiency (245s/27 tools with skill vs 365s/29 tools without, where the baseline re-ran all four package suites fresh out of turbo-cache distrust) and no assertion measures that.

suggestions.assertion: Ran pnpm test and caught the i18n parity failure for the missing pt-BR 'labelLimitReached' key
suggestions.reason: The wording conflates the command with the outcome. The baseline caught the failure via a targeted 'pnpm --filter @openkeep/web test -- parity' before ever running full pnpm test — same genuine outcome, different command. Reword to something like 'the verification caught the missing pt-BR twin via the repo's test suite before any ready verdict' or, if the intent is that full pnpm test must be the detector, say so explicitly.

No assertion covers verification efficiency or redundant re-runs. Consider an assertion like 'did not re-run unchanged package suites after a green cached result' — in this iteration that is the clearest observable difference the skill produced.

eval_feedback.overall: Run is clean and fully corroborated (5/5), but the eval's assertions are all satisfied by the baseline too; the discriminating signal (fewer redundant runs, faster gate, skill-ordered report) is currently unmeasured.
